reviewer: Specialist: life_safety, accessibility, acoustics_av (other disciplines not scored)
weighted_score_note: Weighted over the three assigned disciplines only (15/10/10, normalised to 35). Not comparable to a full nine-discipline score.

critical_blockers.finding: The two stage-side hall exits are labelled 'protected route to BOH exits', but they lead into a 3.0 m BOH corridor that has no external door. The only ways out of the corridor are 1.2 m single room doors (FireExit=False) into the vestry/pastors' office, which leads to DR-EXT-BOH-1, or into the MEP plant room, which leads to DR-EXT-BOH-2. About 1,011 hall occupants are assigned to these routes (635 and 406 at the final doors). By the design's own 5 mm/person placeholder those room doors would need 3.18 m and 2.03 m, but they give 1.12 m effective. EGR-08 checks only the external doors and misses this bottleneck. The route is obstructed and its capacity is overstated.
critical_blockers.evidence: manifest: DR-STAGE-W (x 21.4) and DR-STAGE-E (x 67.7) at y 50.55, props Role '...protected route to BOH exits'; SP-BOH-C corridor y 50.7-53.7 with no external door (ENV-WALL-BOH-W/E solid); DR-EXT-BOH-1 at (4.0, 59.55) inside SP-BOH-01 Vestry (x 0.15-10); DR-EXT-BOH-2 at (76, 59.55) inside SP-BOH-08 plant room (x 64-79.85); DR-BOH-01 / DR-BOH-08 EffectiveClearWidth 1.12, FireExit False; exit_schedule.csv DR-STAGE-W 620, DR-STAGE-E 391; geometry_checks EGR-08 loads BOH-1 635, BOH-2 406. open_issues.md says the corridor 'would need protection', which contradicts the 'protected route' label.

findings.finding: See B-CB-01. The stage-side exits discharge through the vestry office and the plant room via 1.2 m single doors, so about 30 % of the hall's egress has no workable route.
findings.fix: Run the BOH corridor through to external doors at both ends: put 3.6 m external door sets in the corridor end walls (ENV-WALL-BOH-W/E), or line them up with the north ends of the ambulatories, so the corridor discharges directly outside. Make the corridor a fire-separated route, with wall and door ratings set by the fire engineer, and either stop the plant-room door opening onto it or move the plant room. Remove 'protected' from the door Role until the protection is designed. Extend EGR-08 to check every door along the route, not only the external door.

findings.finding: Two thirds of hall occupants (2,267 of 3,383) must leave at the +2.98 m rear passage and go down stairs (6 stairs of 18 risers). Only 4 exits are at grade, and 2 of those are the compromised BOH exits. The shallow-rake fan therefore depends on stairs more than Option A does (1,145 occupants from +4.42).
findings.evidence: exit_schedule.csv L02 exits: W-REAR 208, E-REAR 239, S1 504, S2 516, ARC-W 400, ARC-E 400; L00: W-FRONT 68, E-FRONT 37, STAGE-W 620, STAGE-E 391.
findings.fix: Add grade-level exits at the ends of the cross-aisle passage (+0.41 m), for example external doors in the side walls beside the front corners, where the cross-end stairs already land at grade. Rebalance so that no more than about half of the occupants use stairs.

findings.finding: Every L02 egress stair is a single straight flight of 18 risers (0.166 m) with no intermediate landing. The 6.0 m foyer stairs have handrails only at their outer edges. The 2.4 m ambulatory stairs take up more than half of the 4.5 m ambulatory, which is also the step-free route and the onward route to DR-EXT-AMB-W2/E2 (608 and 639 occupants).
findings.evidence: geometry_checks.json stairs: ARC-STAIR-FOYER-W/E width 6.0, ARC-STAIR-CORNER-W/E 3.0, ARC-STAIR-AMB-W/E 2.4, all 18 risers x 0.166; layout.py foyer() and ambulatories() place rails at x0+0.05 and x0+sw-0.05 only; params ambulatory width 4.5; EGR-08 loads AMB-W2 608 / AMB-E2 639.
findings.fix: Break each flight into 2 x 9 risers with a landing. Add central handrails on stairs wider than about 2.4 m. Widen the ambulatory beside its stair, or move the side stair out of the ambulatory, so that at least 2.4 m stays clear past the stair foot.

findings.finding: Travel distances exceed the placeholder flag (406 occupants over 30 m, max 41.6 m). The egress engine also understates the routes. It measures the final leg as a straight line from the hall door to the external door, ignoring the dog-leg along the BOH corridor and through the room doors, and it adds a fixed 6.0 m for any stair, whatever its length. The comparison script measures a maximum direct seat-to-exit distance of 30.89 m (A: 26.1 m).
findings.evidence: layout.py egress(): finals = min Euclidean distance to ext_doors + (0 or 6.0 m stair); EGR-03 {max 41.6, over_flag 406}; comparison.md direct seat-to-exit max 30.89.
findings.fix: Route the final legs on a corridor/stair network graph (stair slope length, landings, door positions) and re-report EGR-03/04.

findings.finding: Wheelchair users get some of the worst views in the room. The six front places sit at or behind the pulpit line, about 82-99 deg off the pulpit axis, which is beyond the 85 deg limit used to trim congregation seats. The end band groups M01 and M12 are about 85-90 deg off. SGT-H1 does not catch this because it checks congregation chairs only.
findings.evidence: accessible_positions.csv FW-01 (31.00, 42.06), FW-02 (31.44, 40.74), FW-03 (32.07, 39.49), FE mirror; ARC-PULPIT at (40.0, 40.6); M01-01 (17.54, 40.40), M12-02 (62.46, 40.40); params seating.max_bearing_from_pulpit_deg 85; layout.py sightline_checks loops over self.seats only.
findings.fix: Move the front places into the central front blocks (within 45 deg of the pulpit axis) and the band places from the two outermost groups towards the centre blocks. Extend SGT-H1 and the bearing check to wheelchair positions.

findings.finding: Both the step-free route to the 24-place band and the escape route from it depend on the sloped radial front aisles: about 11 m long, up to 1:13.6, running between chairs with no handrails or landings. The egress model sends band occupants out via the ends of the cross-aisle passage, but those ends are 3-riser stairs (ARC-STAIR-CROSS-W/E, 0.137 m), not ramps. So the model's own evacuation route for wheelchair users goes down steps, and the only step-free way out is back down a seating aisle against the flow of people. The end ramps (ARC-RAMP-BAND-W/E, 0.10 m rise, 1.2 m run) only lift users from the passage onto the band.
findings.evidence: geometry_checks ACC-03 route text; stairs ARC-STAIR-CROSS-W/E 3 risers x 0.137; layout.py egress() routes the 'cross' passage via self.corner_ramps, which choir_zones() builds as stairs; GEO-02 1:13.6; params accessibility._route 'Corner ramps were tried and removed'.
findings.fix: Replace the cross-aisle end stairs with 1:12 ramps down to the front-corner floor (0.41 m rise, about 4.9 m run plus landings), or with a level link to new side-wall exits at +0.41 m with external ramps (as in Option A ACC-06). Then allow wheelchair occupants only step-free links in the egress model.

findings.finding: The lift reaches L02 (rear passage and booth), but L02 has no wheelchair places and no refuge spaces, so a wheelchair user who goes up by lift has nowhere safe to wait beside the six stair heads.
findings.evidence: ARC-LIFT / DR-LIFT-L02 (1.84 m clear); accessible_positions.csv has no L02 entries; no refuge zones in the manifest.
findings.fix: Add refuge spaces at the foyer stair heads, or state that L02 is not a wheelchair destination and why.

findings.finding: The hall wall behind the rear passage is a faceted concave arc centred on the platform focus F (radius about 44 m, 10 deg facets about 7.7 m long). Facets that large do not break up the focusing, so sound from the platform will come back to the platform as a concentrated echo about 250 ms later. The infill above the wall is not modelled.
findings.evidence: layout.py rear_corners(): ARC-WALL-ARC-* on radius R_out + t about F, arc_wall_facet_deg 10; open_issues.md 'acoustic infill above the faceted rear-passage wall ... not modelled'.
findings.fix: Make the rear arc wall and its infill highly absorptive or diffusing (convex, at 1-2 m scale), or angle the facets so that each reflects down into the rear rows instead of back towards F. Ask the acoustician for an early ray-trace.

findings.finding: At 27,968 m3 (9.3 m3 per seat) the volume suits amplified worship and is better than A's 16.6 m3 per seat. However, the low 5 deg mono-pitch roof (top 14.2 m) is a large hard surface almost parallel to the floor, and the side walls of the 80 m fan send strong side reflections to the outermost (85 deg) seats. No RT or early-reflection estimate has been made.
findings.evidence: comparison.md hall volume 27,968 m3, 9.32 m3/seat, roof top 14.2; params structure roof_pitch_deg 5.
findings.fix: Provide an absorptive roof soffit or ceiling zone over the rear half and treat the side walls. Obtain an RT estimate before fixing the roof build-up.

findings.finding: The loudspeaker concept for a 170 deg fan (left, centre and right arrays at y 34-36 plus two out-fills at x 20/60) is plausible, but coverage has not been checked. The 320 seats beyond 75 deg from the pulpit depend on the out-fills and the side IMAG screens. 1,398 seats rely on screens, and SGT-H1 checks only horizontal angle and distance. It does not check vertical angle, or whether the choir, platform party or trusses block the view.
findings.evidence: manifest SRV-AV-SPK-MAIN-L (31.0, 36.3, 6.5), MAIN-C (40.8, 34.3, 5.8), OUT-W (20, 32.3, 6.2); SRV-AV-SCREEN-SIDE-W (20, 45.8, 5.15, yaw -55); SGT-H1 relying_on_screens 1398; comparison.md seats > 75 deg 320.
findings.fix: Run a simple direct-sound coverage map over all 3,000 seats (angle off each speaker's axis and loss with distance). Add vertical-angle and obstruction checks to SGT-H1.

strengths: The volume per seat (9.3 m3) and the shorter maximum pulpit distance (39.5 m vs 57.6 m) favour speech intelligibility and amplified worship.
There are 10 hall exits with 35.6 m of capacity width against a 22.58 m placeholder demand (EGR-01/06), and no occupant is over the 60 m total flag (EGR-04).
C-values pass everywhere (0.0602 / 0.1203), the band C-value is 0.107, and no seat is more than 60 deg off its facing direction (head turn at most 23.7 deg).
There are 30 wheelchair places in 14 groups with companion seats, step-free choir places, five accessible WCs and a lift to L02.
The open issues honestly flag that the BOH corridor needs protection and that acoustics and AV are not designed.
limitations: Positions for the cited doors, spaces, stairs and AV items were taken from the manifest matrices and openings. I did not re-run the egress engine on a route graph, so the true BOH-route distances and the evacuation times for band users are not quantified. I did no acoustic modelling; echo delays are first-order estimates (2 x 44 m / 343 m/s). I did not review the renders in detail. No local code values were available, so every width, riser and distance criterion is a placeholder.
certification_disclaimer: This is a concept-stage QA review score. It is not professional certification, fire/egress approval, accessibility audit, acoustic design or code-compliance confirmation; a qualified fire engineer, access consultant and acoustician must review the design under applicable Zimbabwean requirements.
